question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution empowers the President of India to issue an ordinance when both the Houses of Parliament are NOT in session?
solution:
The correct answer is** __123.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** President may issue the ordinances** that he believes are required if, at any time other than when both Houses of Parliament are in session, he is** convinced that circumstances** exist that need him to act immediately.
 
• The **President of India has the authority** to enact laws when one of the two Houses of Parliament is not in session under** Article 123** of the Indian Constitution. 
 
• An** ordinance may address** any issue that the Parliament has the authority to legislate on and is subject to the same legislative restraints as the Parliament in accordance with the delegation of authority between the **Union, State, and Concurrent Lists.**​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **prohibitions on courts looking into parliamentary** procedures are covered in** Article 122**.

 
 
• It also specifies that any purported procedural irregularity cannot be used to bring into doubt the legality of any **proceedings in Parliament.**
 
 
 
• The restriction on **Parliamentary discussion is mentioned in Article 121 **of the Indian Constitution. It specifies that no discussion of the behaviour of any Supreme Court or **High Court **Judge in the course of his duties shall take place in Parliament until there is a motion to present an address to the President asking for the **Judge's removal as set forth below. **
 
• The** establishment and composition of the Supreme Court** are covered in **Article 124.** It stipulates that there will be a Chief Justice of India and up to seven additional judges, until a greater number is prescribed by law, on the **Supreme Court of India.**
